title: Manila declares leptospirosis epidemic

blocks.text: Manila has declared a leptospirosis epidemic after cases rose beyond the city’s set danger level, with several city-run hospitals now reaching full capacity amid the continued influx of patients. "We surpass the epidemic threshold for leptospirosis," the city government announced. Manila OIC-City Health Officer Dr. Grace Padilla reported the development to Mayor Francisco “Isko” Moreno Domagoso on Monday, Sept. 7, saying the city is now in an “epidemic condition” due to the rising number of leptospirosis cases. Based on data from the Manila Health Department (MHD), the city’s attack rate for leptospirosis jumped to 3.48 percent from 1.27 percent last week, indicating a rapid increase in cases within a short period. Padilla also reported that several city government district hospitals have reached full capacity due to the continued influx of patients. These include Ospital ng Maynila, Sta. Ana Hospital, and Justice Jose Abad Santos General Hospital. Following the report, Domagoso directed city government agencies to intensify the city’s campaign against leptospirosis, particularly among residents who were exposed to floodwaters in recent weeks. The city government will also step up its public information campaign to inform residents that free doxycycline capsules are available at all 44 health centers and seven district hospitals under the Manila city government. Domagoso said the city government, through the MHD and its 896 barangays, should proactively reach out to residents affected by flooding and distribute doxycycline to those exposed to floodwaters. He stressed that it would be better for the city government to bring the preventive medicine directly to affected residents as leptospirosis cases continue to rise.
